signal_flow.via: click and cue markers; monitor bus only, never mains

design_rules: No aggregate devices: one interface, the M4.
Loops live in hardware so a computer hiccup cannot kill accumulated loop state.
Buffer stays tight, 64 to 128 samples, for synth latency under the keyboard.

routing_questions.question: Which X32 channels take the looper outs, and what feeds its inputs?
X32 scene: channel map, monitor bus assignments, matrix config for the record feed.

proposed_x32.principle: Keep the doc's flow (M4 to console) and make the looper a send/return: the console keeps separate faders for dry sources and loop returns, loops still live in hardware, and the vocal never has to pass through the looper to reach the PA.

channels.name: Lead Vox
channels.source: vocal mic (SM58/Beta 58) into X32 XLR in 1

buses.name: Looper Send
buses.feeds: aux out 1/2 to RC-505 MK2 INST 1 L/R (post-fader from ch 1, 3, 4; never from ch 5/6 so loops do not re-loop)

buses.name: IEM
buses.feeds: aux out 5/6 to the in-ear pack; ch 7/8 pre-fader; ch 7/8 are NOT assigned to LR

matrix.name: Record
matrix.feeds: matrix out 1/2 to MOTU M4 inputs 1/2 (LR post-fader copy)

answers.rc505_x32_io: Looper MAIN OUT L/R into X32 ch 5/6. Its INST 1 L/R input is fed from X32 bus 1/2 (aux out 1/2) carrying vocal and synth; the vocal mic goes to the console, not straight into the looper.
answers.x32_scene: Channels 1, 3-8 as above; bus 1/2 looper send; bus 5/6 in-ears with click/cue never on LR; matrix 1/2 record feed to the M4.

caveats: The .scn artifact carries channel names, colors, and icons only. Bus, matrix, and LR assignments are written here as instructions and must be set on the console by hand on first load.
Loading a scene on the real console is refused by the machine; the operator loads it.
